name: Chthonic-Dirge
description: The sea here is thick with dissolved metals, so sunsets burn green and gold above the waves. Beneath them wait towering mountain ranges, and everything the light never reaches.

The air carries cold salt and iodine, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts. Fossil beds suggest rich seas once flourished here; now the chemistry records only a slow suffocation.
The oldest impact basin predates the system's estimated age by a comfortable margin. The survey bureau has quietly stopped publishing the numbers.

For traders, exotic matter, medicinal compounds and biomass alone justifies the crossing; for everyone else, the planet pays in questions. Fuel is cheap, information is not, and both are dangerous to carry.
